reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 20 feet of water using minnows.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to transition away from summertime offshore patterns of using Texas rigged worms. Crappie are schooled up on main lake brush piles and deep grass lines in 12-20 feet of water hitting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: There is a good bass bite targeting deep grass edges with lightweight plastics. Numbers of bass are suspended offshore around bait.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in standing timber with small minnows.
reports.by: Hundley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Early morning bass bite is fair around pond weed with buzz baits and frogs. Crappie are excellent.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Catfishing has also been slow, and black bass action remains sluggish as well.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on the docks, and brush piles 15-30 feet. Largemouth bass are fair using topwaters, crankbaits, spoons on main lake points and deep rock. White bass and hybrids are scattered on main lake humps and points hitting topwaters, slabs or trolling. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 6.13 pounds are good in 3- 5 feet of water on topwater frogs in the shoreline grass with some fish on chatterbaits, crankbaits and jigs in the brush 5-12 feet of water. Crappie are excellent to 14 inches on minnows and jigs off deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and on scattered brush piles in 10-20 feet of water. White bass are slow to 1.50 pounds on crappie jigs and crankbaits out of the lights at night.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling on the main lake and in the river.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: On the other hand, striper and black bass fishing remains slow.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to 3 pounds on small finesse worms in 10-15 feet of water. Crappie good to 2 pounds on jigs and minnows in 10-15 feet of water on the main lake docks and in the timber towards the creek.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are chasing shad schools early off and holding on deeper docks and offshore structure, while breams are stacked thick around docks, brush, and banks from 1-15 feet. Crappie are coming off timber and structure in 13-20 feet, with minnows, hair jigs, and plastics producing, though anglers may need to move often as schools scatter. Hybrid and white bass are schooling on flats and drop-off edges in 13-18 feet, hitting slabs, spoons, and shad.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs over deep water brush piles. Black bass are fair on spinnerbaits and jerkbaits.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good with bigger fish being caught on senkos in 12-15 feet of water, and smaller bass can be caught on square bill crankbaits in shallow water.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: The cooler weather should bring fish shallow and turn on the topwater bass bite. Bass are good early in the morning working underspins on points just off the grass, then rattle traps off the bank later in the morning or Carolina rigs 14-16 feet of water.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: There are still a few groups of fish offshore, but bass are primarily scattered from 12-22 feet in roadbeds, humps and long points. Bass are schooling in creeks, so a hard-bodied popper should work. Lake Fork crappie fishing is heating back up as we begin to head into early fall. The black crappie are stacking up in huge numbers this week on brush piles and other structures. The white crappie are also showing up on timber along creek channels in 18-28 feet.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in shallow water with topwater, spinnerbaits, buzz bait, chatterbaits or worms. Crappie are slow with minnows or jigs in brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: As the weather cools, bass should transition to shallow water to feed on bait fish. Reports of bass biting in the San Gabriel River above the steps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting on brush piles out in 15 feet of water using minnows. Bass are feeding on shad in the back of pockets.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing continues to be excellent on small minnows and jigs. Largemouth bass are good on shallow crankbaits near main lake points. Some good topwater action is reported early and late as bass push shad to the banks.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair up the river around timber on worms and crankbaits. Crappie are good on minnows fished over structure in 4-13 feet of water. White bass are fair on slab spoons fished over humps and ridges.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Bounce slabs off the bottom when fish are on structure.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting well in the East Fork, holding tight to structure in 12-14 feet of water and hitting minnows or small hand-tied jigs, especially before 10 a.m. Largemouth bass are active in the mornings on darker-colored grubs, Texas-rigged worms, crankbaits, and spinnerbaits in the shallows, then move to boat docks and offshore brush later in the day, where worms and crankbaits off deeper points can be productive.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: As the weather cools, bass should transition to shallow water to feed on bait fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with many smaller sized fish in soft plastics in brush piles. Crappie are on brush piles biting minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: As the weather cools, bass should transition to shallow water to feed on bait fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught in less than two feet of water with topwater. Keep your eyes peeled for surfacing bass and cast a lipless crankbait or topwater. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20 feet of water on brush piles with orange and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good with a white spinnerbait in the mornings around shallow structure. Crappie bite has been fair in brush piles around 18 feet of water.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, spoons, spinnerbaits and live bait are working. Crappie are slow to fair in 10-28 feet of water. Largemouth are sitting around shallow rocks and brush pretty well through the day.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: As the weather cools, bass should transition to shallow water to feed on bait fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in coves using chatterbaits, swimbaits and Texas rigged worms. Crappie are scattered suspended in standing timber.
reports.by: Hambone fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass and smallmouth bass are great with white crankbaits, green jointed repalas and topwater lures. Crappie are fair in Sanford Yake, North Canyon, and Fritch Fortress with pearl white and pearl blue, grey or yellow jigs.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good from the pier with nice size catches reported. Quality sized bass are good in 2-5 feet of water with spinnerbaits, crankbaits and buzzbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on white swim jigs, bladed jigs, and walking topwaters in the shallow water. Bass are starting to school offshore in 12-15 feet of water on hard spots, so cast Carolina rigs, or crankbaits. Crappie are excellent in 12-18 feet of water with bigger fish in timber, and smaller fish in the brush with crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: The summer pattern has returned, leaving bass in a bit of a funk and seemingly confused about whether to stay deep or move shallow, making the fall transition uncertain. Crappie populations remain strong, while catfish are running slow. Largemouth bass are excellent on small topwaters, or small swimbaits cast into schooling bass midlake. Bass are feeding up for the winter. Crappie are excellent on the biggest brush piles you can find. The best lure has been white and chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass continue to be fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Bass are holding back in the shade around heavy cover to escape the sun. Early morning and late evening topwater is also effective for targeting bass. Crappie were fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are suspended 3-4 feet below the surface over brush in 15 feet of water. Crappie are preferring minnows. No reports of largemouth bass.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up 9 pounds. Crappie good in Big Trees suspended down 7/8 ft.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie good in 8-16 feet of water on brush, timber and boathouses using hand tied jigs. Bass are good around boathouses and vegetation at the backs of creeks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Drum crappie are still biting in deep water on minnows around boat docks and brush piles. Black bass are elusive.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with small swimbaits cast into schools, or medium diving crankbaits for smaller fish related to the bottom of points. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Fish are feeding on very small shad so downsize your swimbaits, slabs and topwater baits. The crappie bite has picked up nicely. Largemouth bass are crushing topwater at first light, then shifting to shallow crankbaits around dock legs as the sun climbs.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Bass continue to bite well early in the mornings when the weather is still cool. Anglers are finding success with chatter baits and Texas-rigged worms around lily pads, fallen trees, and other cover, with recent reports of two 4-pounders and 6-pound largemouth caught on chatter baits within the past two weeks.
reports.by: Aric Brooks, Huntsville State Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass can be caught in brush piles on the docks.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Water temperature is around 90 degrees, and bass are being caught shallow on points and pockets with topwater frogs and senkos, while crankbaits are working on points and drains and jigs or Carolina rigs are producing off ledges and structure. Crappie are starting to stack up on brush and timber, white bass are schooling off points, and catfish have moved into deeper water and creek channels with cut bait working well.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite has slowed at the marina, but bluegill remain fair with crickets and worms, and catfish remain good with minnows or punch bait. The crappie are fair with jigs or minnows over brush in 8-15 feet of water. Black bass are slow on crankbaits and soft plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Quality sized bass are good in 2-5 feet of water with soft plastics. Crappie are fair with fish scattered in mid depths.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Some smaller, schoolie-sized largemouth surfacing, but the action is light and spread far and wide. A small, clear soft plastic on a jighead cast fast and accurately is about the only thing these shad-eating bass will respond to consistently.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been slow. Largemouth bass are picking up and we are seeing fish feeding at daylight and dusk.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is slow right now but catfish action has been good on jug lines and trotlines.
reports.by: Chad Kinsfather, Lavaca Navidad River Authority

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Locate bass on docks and structure as the water cools off and fish start to feed more frequently. Smallmouth bass are staging off the banks on points with structure in 15-25 feet of water. Stripers continue to be hit-or-miss with the best bite on topwaters switching to slabs later in the day.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be targeted locating drains containing brush in 15-20 feet throwing weedless baits such as Texas rig drop shot has been working well.
reports.by: Tyler Torwick, Torwick's Guiding Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Catfish are scattered with a good bite on liver Crappie are good on minnows in 16-20 feet of water on brush piles. Bass are good on trick worms, spinnerbaits and crankbaits. Some catches of bass on topwater.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on structure in 12-20 feet of water with live bait, or purple and chartreuse 1/16 ounce jigs. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits. Crappie are fair on brush piles with minnows and shad.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: Crappie will start roaming as the weather cools.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush piles with minnows or hand tied jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early in the morning and evening in shallow water against the cattails. Crappie and sand bass are slow, with few anglers targeting the species.
reports.by: Michael James, local angler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in the timber off of the main channel in 12-18 feet of water with hair jigs or minnows.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is slow with fish hanging around the main body of water with a lot of schooling activity. Crappie are great as fish begin to put on more weight for winter and big schools of crappie can be found around brush and timber around river and creek channels.
reports.by: Cade Rudiger, local angler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow and the crappie are slow.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great in areas with milfoil grass. Flipping docks or working rocks along the deep edges will catch some bigger bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on live minnows or small jigs staying tight to trees.
reports.by: Hundley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in timber, brush and around docks with jigs or minnows.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: There is a good shallow bass bite in 2-4 feet around pond weed early morning with a topwater lure with a cupped propellor tail or buzzbaits. Crappie are excellent.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on docks, and brush piles in 15-30 feet of water with minnows. Largemouth bass are fair to good with topwaters, crankbaits, and spoons on main lake points and deep rock. White bass and hybrids are good on main lake humps and points with topwaters, slabs or trolling. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 6.68 pounds are good in 3-5 feet of water on weedless hollow body topwater frogs in the shoreline grass with some fish on crankbaits and jigs in 5-12 feet of water on brush. Crappie are good, with some fish up to 14 inches, on minnows and jigs off deeper large docks with brush on the main lake, and on scattered brush piles in 10-15 feet of water. White bass are slow to 1.50 pounds on crappie jigs and crankbaits out of the lights at night and some schooling action in the open water of the main lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is improving on brush piles and offshore structures with finesse style baits.
reports.by: The Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in standing timber and brush piles in 20 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Captain Aaron Dick, One Up Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been tough due to the full moon and slower water current. Bass are slow with a few bites using flukes and topwater plugs in the lily pads with birds. Look for shad or birds at the cuts and turns in the river for schools of bass using a Texas rig junebug worm or junebug colored dropshot.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striper and black bass remain slow, but redfish action is excellent with fish ranging from 5-10 pounds and bigger, caught trolling or casting silver and gold spoons and H&H plastics in various parts of the lake, especially in 15-25 feet of water where large schools are showing up.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing continues to be slow, but you can flip grass and catch some good fish.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing Tours

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Consistently finding the best hybrid action in 13-18 feet of water with slabs, and spinnerbaits using the proven saw tooth retrieve technique.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck's Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing is good, with white bass and crappie active, and channel and blue catfish biting excellent.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow but can be targeted in the cattails with reaction baits. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is very slow, while crappie are fair, with decent action coming off brush piles.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in 15-30 feet of water on or near the bottom.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in 12-25 feet of water on brush and docks with hand tied jigs or minnows 12- 25 feet of water.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass and black bass are slow.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is slowly improving with occasional limits, though many catches are still juvenile fish. Bass action has been good in 3-15 feet along hard, rocky bottoms on Texas rigs, crankbaits, shaky heads, and football jigs.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early in the morning working underspins on points just off the grass, then rattle traps off the bank later in the morning or Carolina rigs 14-16 feet of water. Later in the day use deep diving crankbaits off points for 3-4 pound bass.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on the main lake early in the day with topwaters, chatterbaits and square bill crankbaits until the midday sun.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are slow with minnows or jigs in brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Reports of bass biting in the San Gabriel River above the steps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 14 feet of water on brush with minnows and jigs. Bass are slow biting early and late in shallow water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is good to excellent on small jigs and small minnows fished from in town to near Waters edge. Largemouth bass are being caught in numbers with an occasional fish to 5 pounds. Topwater catches are good early and late for largemouth bass.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on worms and crankbaits. Crappie are good on jigs tipped with crappie nibbles. White bass are fair on slab spoons fished over humps and points.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are holding near cypress trees along drop-offs, hitting grubs and Texas-rigged worms early, then moving under docks later in the day where crankbaits and spinnerbaits in the 4-6 foot zone work best. Crappie are biting in the East Fork, Luces Bayou, and West Fork near deeper structure, with white and blue jigs or minnows on gold hooks working well.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with many smaller sized fish catches soft plastics in brush piles. Crappie are on brush piles biting minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting soft plastics on brush in 8-20 feet of water. Schooling bass are hitting topwater or swimbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good with limits possible, when the water temperature cools the bite will improve as fish start feeding up. Target crappie in 10-18 feet of water with structure in 15-18 feet being the sweet spot. Bass are good in 5-20 feet of water on rock or concrete structures, such as boat, ramps, riprap, and bridges. In the morning bass can be as shallow as 2 feet hugging the bank. Bass are not attacking swimbaits. Use a white or chartreuse 1 ounce slab with a jig tied approximately 18 inches above to produce two fish on one rod.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20 feet of water on brush piles with orange and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. There is good topwater bass action in the morning.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 8-15 feet of water on offshore brush, power lines, and standing timber with minnows. Largemouth bass are good on offshore brush, docks, bulkheads and rocks in 4-12 feet of water with Texas rigs, spinnerbaits, or Carolina rigs.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair along the hydrilla with senkos, vibrating jigs and swimbaits. Crappie are fair fishing areas without brown bubbles.
reports.by: Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good from the pier with nice size catches reported.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent moving shallow with lots of schooling activity. Target bass in 3-8 feet of water with a bladed jig or swim jig. Crappie are good in 12-18 feet of water with bigger fish in timber, and smaller fish in the brush with crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: The summer pattern has returned, leaving bass in a bit of a funk and seemingly confused about whether to stay deep or move shallow, making the fall transition uncertain. Crappie populations remain strong, while catfish are running slow. Largemouth bass are good, roaming midlake in large schools. Cast small topwater lures, small paddle tails, or small fluke over schooling bass. Crappie are excellent with limits possible with 1/32 ounce white and chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Bass are holding back in the shade around heavy cover to escape the sun. Early morning and late evening topwater is also effective for targeting bass. Crappie were fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are shallow or suspended in the water column 3-6 feet below the surface above brush. Crappie are preferring minnows. No reports of largemouth bass.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good with catches up to 9 pounds possible in 10-12 feet of water in thick brush. Crappie are good on minnows around timber in both rivers with minnows.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on brush. Bass are slow with soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slowly moving to the backs of creeks hitting jigs, but can still be caught flipping weightless worms under docks. Crappie are good on brush in 12-18 feet of water on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting in deep water around docks and brush piles on minnows.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good, slowly fishing a solid white crappie jig. Crappie ranging from 1-1.5 pounds can be found in 15-20 fish groups in standing timber. Bass are good on dropshots and large swimbaits on main points or suspended in the middle of the lake.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Slab spoons, swimbaits, and downriggers are all producing, so keep a mix of gear ready. The crappie bite has picked up nicely. Largemouth bass are crushing topwater at first light, then shifting to shallow crankbaits around dock legs as the sun climbs.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and relating to brush piles in 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are at some bridge columns.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on timber in 12-18 feet of water with minnows or natural colored or silver and chartreuse jigs. Largemouth bass are good offshore, and secondary points at the mouths of creeks with jigs or shad imitation baits. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass can be caught around docks using a variety of lures.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: The marina bite continues to have a consistent fair crappie bite, fair bluegill bite with crickets and worms, and good catfish bite with minnows or punch bait. Main lake crappie are fair with jigs or minnows over brush in 8-15 feet of water. Black bass are fair on crankbaits and soft plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: A few bass can be caught with topwaters, but the strong action is still right around the corner as the shad activity increases. When 60 degree mornings become the norm the crappie bite will improve, until then the bite is slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Some smaller, "schoolie"-sized largemouth have turned up doing some surface feeding, but it is light and spread far and wide. A small, clear soft plastic on a jighead cast fast and accurately is about the only thing these shad-eating bass will respond to consistently.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Slab spoons, downriggers and swimbaits are working equally well. The crappie bite has picked up. The largemouth bass bite is good on frogs at daylight.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Live bait and slabs are working on shallow flats and ledges off the main lake in 15-25 feet of water. Crappie are biting jigs or minnows on points with stumps and brush in 12-20 feet of water, or docks and shade in coves. Stripers are hit-or-miss with the best bite on topwaters or slabs on flats in 10-20 feet of water or deep in 60 feet of water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Crappie remain slow on brush piles and natural timber in 16-22 feet, with most caught on live bait rather than jigs.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass continue to have a soft bite, so fish slowly with bigger brush hogs, big worms, and dropshots. Target brush near deep water for some bass up to 3 pounds. As the water continues to cool bass will start chasing bait into the creeks. Bass are good working flooded brush or grass with worms, creature baits and even a frog early to get some great bites. Early morning bass bite throwing swimbaits, squarebill crankbaits, and spinnerbaits around brush in 5-10 feet of water close to main lake points.
reports.by: Randal Frisbee, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows on brush in 16-20 feet of water. Crappie are starting to scatter in the shallows to feed. Bass are good on crankbaits, trick worms, or topwaters.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits and jigs. Crappie are fair on brush piles with minnows and shad.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are up in the main lake in brush 15-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass fishing is good using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in 10-25 feet of water on brush piles, rocks piles and main made objects. Crappie are in 10-25 feet of water on brush piles. Target brush piles without bass for crappie.
reports.by: Cade Rudiger, local angler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has picked up quite a bit in the last couple of weeks. A lot of bait is out in the river channel with bass feeding on them.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, black bass, and stripers have been slow, but bank fishing has produced some solid redfish catches using live tilapia, shrimp, and crawfish.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is good on the bridge, shallower docks and brush piles. Largemouth bite is decent with early morning topwaters then switching over to jigs, medium crankbaits and Texas rigged baits near docks and main lake points. White bass and hybrids are good on main lake humps with slabs or trolling. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Black bass and stripers remain slow, but bank fishing has been very productive, with redfish, blue catfish, and channel catfish taken on live tilapia and cut bait from multiple areas around the lake.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been tough, but you can flip grass and catch some good fish.
reports.by: Evan Coleman

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing has been productive across parts of the lake with good reports of channel and blue catfish, along with some white bass, crappie, and black bass being caught.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is slow overall, with most action coming on soft plastics in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been fair on deeper docks and structure as well as chasing bait on ledges up to 20 feet deep. Crappie are better, folks are picking up decent catches, finding them on structure and timber in 13-21 feet. Hybrids and whites are schooling well and providing good action, being productive using slabs, spoons or shad, finding them on flats and the edge of drop-offs in 14-21 feet.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is slowly improving, with many juveniles being caught and a few solid keepers showing up in 20 feet of water on man-made brush piles or submerged timber, with live shad, jigs, and minnow-style grubs working well. Bass reports have been limited.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Early and late bass topwater bite around grasslines and isolated cover on main lake and secondary points. Bass are beginning to school, a hard-bodied popper should work well.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good to excellent midlake on slabs, spinners and trolled Pet Spoons. Largemouth bass are good to 7 pounds on spinners, crankbaits and soft plastics worked near creek entrances and on humps and ridges midlake. Crappie are excellent on small jigs and small minnows fished from in-town to Ports O‘Call.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on worms and crankbaits. Crappie are good on jigs tipped with Berkley Crappie Nibbles. White bass are fair on slab spoons fished over humps and points.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Topwater early and late will produce good black bass and bream action.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are grouping under boat docks and biting well from mid-morning into the afternoon on grubs and worms in dark and light colors, with pink working best early. Crappie are holding deeper in 10-14 feet in Luces’ Bayou and the East Fork, but with muddy water from recent rains, anglers need to put jigs or minnows right in front of them.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, spoons, spinners and live bait are working. Crappie are slow to fair in 10-28 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: The lake is sitting half a foot above full pool, and recent heavy rains combined with unusually cool weather have disrupted the summer pattern, leaving bass scattered and a bit sluggish. Crappie populations remain strong, though catfish action has been slow.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush in 12-18 feet of water on minnows. Bass are fair but a few can be caught flipping baits under docks in the shade, or on ledges with senkos.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow, try Carolina rigged worms on ledges or shaded areas. Crappie are good around docks, brush piles and tree limbs in deep water.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow due to population, but the fishery is recovering.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Water temperatures are finally starting to fall, beginning around 80 degrees in the mornings and climbing to 84-86 degrees during the day, and bass fishing is picking up nicely from shallow to deep water. No crappie reports have come in this week.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: There continues to be a decent bass bite in the grass with lightweight Texas rig worms fished slowly along the edges.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite is best with topwater frogs on pond weeds and poppers at the edge as well as flukes and Yum Dingers.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Water normal stain; 91 degrees; Redfish are fair, with some action around the warm water plant and in the shallows on live tilapia, gold, and silver spoons, H&H plastics, Hoagie Baits, and Bass Assassin plastics. Catfish, black bass, and stripers remain slow across the lake.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is good on the bridge, shallower docks and brush piles. Largemouth bite is fair with early morning topwaters then switching over to jigs, medium crankbaits and Texas rigged baits near docks and main lake points. White bass and hybrids are good on main lake humps with slabs or trolling. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 5.09 pounds in the grass on topwater frogs and in 8-15 feet of water on shaky heads with green pumpkin F5 worms, dropshots with 6-inch worms in Morning Glory, whopper ploppers and square bill crankbaits. Crappie are fair to 13 inches on minnows and jigs in 10-20 feet on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and on scattered brush piles. White bass are fair to 1.25 pounds on crappie jigs and minnows out of the lights at night with some schooling action early and late.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Black bass and stripers remain slow.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: However, bank fishing has been good in parts of the lake, with anglers catching blue and channel catfish, crappie, white bass, and freshwater drum on shrimp, stink bait, and Fish Bites.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: There are some black bass being caught, but really hard to find. Crappie are excellent to 14 inches on minnows in 8-15 feet under docks in Rattlesnake Cove on the right side going in.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is fair, with most catches coming around timber and some being taken early off extended points.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been OK on deeper docks and structure as well as chasing bait on ledges up to 20 feet deep. Crappie are better, folks are picking up decent catches, finding them on structure and timber in 13-21 feet. Hybrids and whites are schooling well and providing good action, being productive using slabs, spoons or shad, finding them on flats and the edge of drop-offs in 14-21 feet.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early on topwaters and frog around grass or pond weeds.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing continues to be the best choice on Granbury on small jigs and minnows. Crappies are being caught from Indian Harbor to the Shores near 15 ft humps and suspended on any kind of structure. Black bass are being caught near creek entrances where baitfish are abundant.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are hitting spinnerbaits, crankbaits, and worms around docks and drop-offs, while catfish are decent on fresh shad, chicken liver, and shrimp in the main lake. Crappie were good before the rains and likely moved tight to structure with the cooler temperatures but should rebound by the weekend. White bass are feeding heavily in the early mornings on slabs and swimbaits.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great dragging a worm on main lake points and around structure has been producing the best.
reports.by: Evan Coleman

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, spoons, spinners, and live bait are working. Crappie are slow to fair in 10 to 28 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good along the hydrilla with swimbaits, weightless senkos and Texas rigged worms. Crappie are good suspended in brush and timber in 25-30 feet using minnows.
reports.by: Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: The lake is sitting 1 foot above pool after recent heavy rains and unseasonably cool weather, which has disrupted the summer pattern and left bass scattered and sluggish. Crappie numbers remain strong, but catfish are slow.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 9 pounds with an 11-pounder reported this week. Crappie are good with limits reported around hardwood trees 15-25 feet suspended.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush in 12-18 feet of water on minnows. Bass are slow but a few are being caught around docks in the shade flipping soft plastics beneath.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow. Crappie are good around docks, brush piles and tree limbs in deep water.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are being caught off main lake docks. Using spinners and slabs on the white bass.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Lots of bass are in the shallows. Crappie r slowly move out to brush and timber.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Catfish are biting well on jug lines and trotlines, while crappie and bass are fair in the upper portion of the lake.
reports.by: Chad Kinsfather, Lavaca Navidad River Authority

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has improved with water temperatures now in the mid-80s. With cooler weather in the forecast next week and highs dropping into the low 80s, expect water temperatures to fall and bass activity to ramp up, setting the stage for a strong fall bite.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Some pretty successful trips staying at one spot for an hour and a half and catching a lot of bass.
reports.by: Randal Frisbee, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on structure in 15-20 feet of water. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are up in the main lake in brush in 15-20 feet of water. White bass fishing is slow on slabs on main lake humps in 25-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass fishing is fair using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good over trees in 15-25 feet on jigs and minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair in 20-35 feet on Carolina rigged and Texas rigged creature baits, fished deep in Wat Red, Kudzu, pumpkinseed, gourd green, and bloodline colors are having the best results.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding more heavily at night than during the day.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Lake Bastrop is fishing decent for bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie limits are possible in 25 feet of water on standing timber with black and green jigs. Black bass are chasing shad and bream. Windy retaining walls will produce marauding bass. Bass are excellent, especially late afternoon.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are hit-or-miss with longer activity on cloudy mornings. Crappie fishing is hot with fish on timber, brush or any structure you can find in 8-25 feet of water. This is definitely a lake to hit up if you are looking for a mess of crappie.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on topwaters early, switch to shad pattern crankbaits as the day warms up. Crappie are good on minnows and jigs at the usual places. Hybrids and sand bass have been good on live bait and slabs. Keep a propeller bait handy for topwater action, a chartreuse slab for when they go deeper.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass up to 5.67 pounds are fair on Hags’s baits with soft plastics and frogs casting into the newly submerged grass and weeds. Crappie are slow with catches up to 10 inches around docks with brush in 9-15 feet of water with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: White bass are surfacing in large schools mid lake hitting slab spoons and topwaters. Crappie are good on brush piles and standing timber in 20-25 feet of water with jigs and minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good throwing shaky heads and Texas-rigged 4-5 inch worms around rock piles to catch some good ones. A medium or deep crankbait will catch some of those bigger bass.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are still in transition from the summer to fall pattern with fish schooling all over the lake.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Hybrids and white bass are good early in the morning at daylight on midlake points and drop offs along sandy flats throughout the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch and the spillway humps in 11-17 feet. Cast spinners and slabs and look for schooling fish on these flats as well as deeper seawalls and shorelines. Use spinnerbaits or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Cast rattle traps, Spoons,Umbrella Rigs, slabs or sassy shads to get the hybrids to bite. The crappie bite has been getting better. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair early in the morning or late in the afternoon on main lake long extended points with shad colored crankbaits and flukes. Crappie are biting on deep docks in 25 feet of water with live minnows or grubs.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have really been doing good on minnows.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow on topwaters early in the morning, or flipping a senko into cattails. Crappie are fair with jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early and late in shallow water and offshore midday on structure and ledges. Crappie are still poor but some can be caught on structure 12-25 feet. Hybrids have been scattered in 13-24 feet with some whites mixed in, some are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs from Bradley Outdoors to jig for them.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass should become more active after the cold front enticing a fall feeding frenzy on points. Bass continue to be good on points hitting squarebill crankbaits early then moving out to 14 feet of water throwing shaky heads and deep diving crankbaits.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Shallow bass bite is good early to mid morning around grass and smaller points in 2-4 feet with topwaters, flukes, or shaky heads and minus 1 type crankbaits. Smaller baits catch numbers, but big worms will catch bigger bass. Bass are aggressive on top water and shallow. The Lake Fork crappie fishing continues to be excellent as we head into fall. Timber still has some great white crappie if you cover water and pick off those fish. Brush piles are holding decent numbers with a combination of white and black crappie. You can find black crappie on underwater road beds and bridges. We should see more and more black crappie on the tops of timber in deeper water over the next month.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are good to excellent on slabs and spinnerbaits in many areas of the lake. Largemouth bass continue to be good on crankbaits and soft plastics fished near humps and ridges near creek entrances. There is a good largemouth bass topwater bite in the back of sloughs where baitfish are holding. Crappie catches are fair to good on small jigs and minnows fished on submerged structures in 10-20 feet of water. Best reports on crappie have been from near Water's Edge to Bent Water.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 7 pounds on worms and crankbaits. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows fished over cover in 4-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Bass are chasing bait fish around the edges of grass. Bead heads will tempt bream and bass, dropping the flies at the front of the grass line.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are really hitting ⅛ ounce grubs rigged weedless in the shallows in the morning. Crappie are fantastic in 8-14 feet of water using hand tied jigs and minnows mainly in large stumps.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is tough with fish scattered. Spotted bass can be caught with crankbaits on brush piles in 10-16 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Activity is picking up daily with shad and small bass in the creeks. There has been a lot of sporadic schooling for white bass and largemouth bass. Crappie can be caught on minnows under the bridges.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the grass near the islands or off the points with a creek channel running on the end of the point.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent on 1/32-1/8 ounce jigs or minnows. Black Bass are in 3-20 feet. Try to hit the main lake points and ledges in 15-20 feet with 1 ounce white slabs for when fish are on the bottom, and topwater plugs, or swimbaits for surfacing fish. Do not be surprised if you catch crappies while you’re trying to catch the gills.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, jigs, and live bait are working. Crappie are fair in 6-26 feet of water. Bass are more active at night. Largemouth bass are slow on jigs and finesse worms. Crappie are heavily stacking up in main lake brush piles in 12-15 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are scattered with some fish suspended on deep brush and some under docks. Crappie action continues to be best on offshore fresh willow tree piles, with some on power line pylons and standing timber.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: White bass are great on roadbeds in 6-16 feet of water hitting Duck Tracker slabs.
reports.by: Michael Richardson, Lake Livingston Adventures

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with red bug worms working the edge of the hydrilla. There are schooling bass along the county line road with best bait the 1/4 ounce chrome rattletrap. Crappie remain excellent in standing timber and brush piles in 25-30 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent with 3-5 pound fish being caught on small swimbaits and topwaters. Crappie are excellent on 1/16 ounce white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are good on topwaters and swimbaits. Crappie are excellent on brush and standing timber in 10-15 feet of water on 1/16 ounce white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow, with one 12 pounder and a 9 pounder reported. Bass are moving around being caught on topwaters, rattle traps and small minnow shad imitating baits. Upper end stained and tough fishing but a few bass being caught on worms. Crappie are good with fish suspended in trees in deeper water hitting minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been fair predominantly from fishing boathouse patterns with spinners, jerks, and finesse type lures. Crappie have been good, but primarily for white crappie down at 16-24 feet on brush and timber, black crappie have been slow.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow. Black bass are slow.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on large or small swimbaits, and dropshots in 10-18 feet of water. Crappie are excellent on 1/16 ounce white crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Fish and a horizontal presentation throwing Bo-Blade slabs and slow rolling. Crappie are fair and relating to brush 15-22 feet deep moving on and off structure, and suspended on the bridge pylons biting minnows.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White Bass fishing remains slow with just a few reports of catches being made on slabs when schools are located off main lake points.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling on points biting Carolina rigs. Crappie are fair on 27 feet on brush piles with minnows over jigs. Target bass with jig head minnows and forward facing sonar. Bass are suspended at the mouth of creeks and on offshores flats chasing bait. When bass are schooling on the bottom cast a Carolina rig, dropshot, and shaky head. Target the hay grass and flooded bushes early in the morning to catch bass chasing bait using a chatterbait, swimbait or frog.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill and catfish are fair. Crappie are slow over brush in8-16 feet of water with jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on soft plastics. Crappie are fair to good on concrete.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Consistent local bass tournament anglers report groups of bass on isolated cover.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is also picking up with the cooler temperatures. Bass fishing is still challenging, but as the water continues to cool, expect fish to move up into the backs of coves and creeks chasing gizzard shad. Smallmouth bass fishing along the bluffs has been productive with live shad, particularly near rocky points in 8-12 feet of water. Switch to slabs after the sun rises in 25 feet or less, but they can be deeper. Numbers of crappie can be caught but very few keepers.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has improved, but forecast is showing lots cooler temperatures so this may slow the bite.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Lake Travis has been good in the morning as you can catch bass feeding shallow in the flooded brush.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with minnows on brush in 16-20 feet of water, and off the barge. Bass are fair on topwater baits, crankbaits and spinner baits in 4-12 feet of water.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of bass have slowed, but fish can be caught with worms, frogs, flukes, and reaction baits. Bass are great right now with frogs around most of the lake. Bass are schooling after shad early in the pockets, so a swimbait, shad colored fluke, shallow crank or vibrating jig/spinnerbait works good for those.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on deep brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass are slow on deeper water ledges with crankbaits and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good 15-22 feet on trees with minnows or jigs.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair suspended in 15-25 feet of water on main and secondary lake points, and ledges are also holding fish.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow, but can be caught on the outside of grass lines with Texas rig worms and weightless flukes. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by, Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good skipping a light Texas rigged worm, creature bait or jig on the docks during the day.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good, target the outside grass lines will catch the best quality bass working a shallow crankbait, fluke or wake. Work the discharge with a shaky head trick worm and dye the tail as bass will eat that all day.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be good in 20 feet of water using live minnows. Largemouth bass and smallmouth bass are shallow around structure using chatterbaits and Texas rigged worms.
reports.by: Benbrook Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie limits are possible in 25 feet of water on standing timber with black and green jigs. Largemouth bass and spotted bass are excellent throwing a walking top water bait near the dam, and good numbers can be caught in shallow pockets and along sea walls with a white buzzbait.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is fair around pond weed and bushes in 2-5 feet with frogs, yellow magics and chatter baits. Points are producing some bass in 6-10 ft on Texas rigs and Carolina rigs. Crappie fishing is hot with fish on timber, brush or any structure you can find in 8-25 feet of water. This is definitely a lake to hit up if you are looking for a mess of crappie.
