reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Topwater baits and chartreuse slabs and spoons should put them in the boat. Crappie fishing continues to be hot. Largemouth bass have been good on topwaters early, square bill cranks as the day warms up.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 4 pounds being caught on buzz baits and frogs in the new water in the grass and weeds. Crappie are slow with 12 inch fish being caught around docks with brush on minnows in 8-12 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent and can be caught with your favorite approach.
reports.by: the Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles and standing timber in 20-25 feet of water with jigs and minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Lake Buchanan is heating up as the bass on this lake love cooler temps and you can catch a bunch piled up on the rock piles throwing swimbaits, crankbaits, and 4-5 inch straight tail worms.
reports.by: Captain Aaron Dick, One Up Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling, so be looking for that and listen for them.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Hybrids and white bass are good early in the morning at daylight on midlake points and drop offs along sandy flats throughout the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch and the spillway humps in 11-17 feet. Cast spinners and slabs and look for schooling fish on these flats as well as deeper seawalls and shorelines. Use spinnerbaits or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Hit up seawalls close to points in depths of 5-18 feet and cast rattle traps, spoons, slabs or sassy shads to get the hybrids to bite. The crappie bite is improving. Target…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with minnows as the weather cools down. Bass are good.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early and late up shallow, and offshore midday on structure and ledges. Crappie are still poor but some can be caught on structure 12-25 feet of water. Hybrids have been scattered in 16-24 feet trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, or using slabs from Bradley Outdoors to jig for them. There is a good morning bass bite in the grass with swimbaits, swim jigs, spooks in white colors, or slow your approach down and throw wacky rigged stick baits in black.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow but can be caught in 3-10 feet of water on the bottom of timber with a crawdad jig.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15 feet of water on minnows. Bass are good, with fish grouping up near isolated pieces of hard cover.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding on points hitting squarebill crankbaits early then moving out to 14 feet of water throwing shaky heads and deep diving crankbaits.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with numbers of fish shallow in 1-2 feet of water around grass hitting spinnerbaits, chatterbaits, and choppos. Lake Fork crappie fishing has been up and down this past week. The white crappie fishing has been the best lately and the black crappie just have not shown up in huge numbers like they will when the water cools off more.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting in shallow water on shad. Crappie are good in the brush on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass to 7 pounds are possible near laydowns and docks near major creek entrances. Crappie action continues to be good on jigs and small minnows fished on submerged structures. Some good crappie action has been on timber north of the railroad bridge.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Bank anglers report catches of smallmouth bass in a cove behind the Silver Lake Marina.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are on cypress trees hitting chatterbaits and light rigged small grubs. Crappie are good tight to structure in East fork and Luces bayou being caught in hand tied jigs and minnows. White bass are really coming back to the south end being caught trolling finally with small power spins and vertical jigging with duck tracker slabs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Good bass can be caught off of isolated laydowns throwing a Texas rigged baby brush hog, or a buzzbait thrown near vegetation on the surface of the water or over submerged hydrilla.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great on 1/32-1/8 th ounce jigs or minnows. Black Bass are in 3-20 feet. Try to hit the main lake points and ledges in 15-20 feet with 1 ounce white slabs for when fish are on the bottom, and topwater plugs, or swimbaits for surfacing fish. Do not be surprised if you catch crappies while you’re trying to catch the gills. Crappie are excellent in 7-20 feet of water in standing timber.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20-25 feet of water over brush piles with jigs or minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good down the edge of hydrilla with swimbaits, weightless senkos and Texas rigged plum colored worms. Bass have been schooling late afternoon near the dam biting 1/4 ounce chrome rattletraps and white buck tailed underspin jigs work good. Crappie are excellent in suspended timber in the 25 feet range.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent for numbers from the bank to 12 feet on a dropshot, straight tailed worm with a light weight, lightly weighted Texas rig, and white and chartreuse spinnerbaits. Crappie are excellent, catching numbers of keepers to fill the freezer on brush piles and standing timber in 12 feet of water.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: If you find bass hugging the bottom in 8-10 feet of water, dragging a Texas rig Mag-worm can be effective. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are good from the bank out to 12 feet on dropshots, lightly weighted Carolina rig, and large swimbaits. Crappie are excellent with light white crappie jig on a split shot rig. Big black crappie up to 1.5 pound are phenomenal.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing ServicesReport by Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing…

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on white chatterbait and spinnerbaits early morning and evening. Flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water midday is the ticket to catch shaded up largemouth bass. Crappie were good around boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass slow but picking up and moving to shallow cover. Crappie are fair suspended 20-25 feet on main lake trees along river channels.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are reporting success using several methods to catch quality bass up to 7 pounds. Bass are being caught on large plastic worms with large shaky heads, and swimbaits. Crappie reports are good with anglers catching limits on live bait and Bone Head jigs.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass, white bass, and hybrid striper fishing should be the most notable improvements, faster moving and deeper lures should be more effective.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow. Bass fishing is slow.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good from the bank to 12 feet around the grass lines with large swimbaits, any soft plastic watermelon red on a Carolina rig or dropshot. Crappie are slow on any translucent colored crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are slow in 10-20 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs or rattle traps. Bass are scattered on ledges, points, and deep timber hitting crankbaits, Carolina rigs, dropshots. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Fish and a horizontal presentation throwing Bo-Blade slabs and slow rolling. Crappie are fair on brush in 15-22 feet of water, and suspended on bridge pylons.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 5-20 foot brush piles and small patches of structure, minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: There continues to be a shallow and a deep bass bite with some schooling action. Bass are fair in shallow water over grass with topwaters, or on secondary points Carolina rigs and dropshots. Crappie are fair on 15-27 feet on brush piles with minnows over jigs. As the weather cools crappie will transition up the river on stumps. Target bass with jig head minnows and forward facing sonar. Bass are suspended at the mouth of creeks and on offshores flats chasing bait. When bass are schooling on the bottom cast a Carolina rig, dropshot, and shaky head. Target the hay grass and flooded bushes early in the morning to catch bass chasing bait using a chatterbait, swimbait or frog.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill and catfish are fair. Crappie are fair over brush in8-16 feet of water with jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow but anglers have reported some success on stick type baits. Slabs and Bomber Slab spoons.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with a 27 pound stringer reported. Crappie are good on brush piles and concrete.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Consistent local bass tournament anglers report that bass are grouped on isolated cover, and having success in short windows under low light conditions right before sunrise and right after sunset.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Also seeing fish in shallow flats drifting live bait and bouncing slabs in 8-15 feet of water on sand flats. Crappie are turning on as water temperatures slowly start to drop. Seeing fish come off structure in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles using crappie minnows and small chartreuse jigs, with darker colors as the lake starts to turn over. Bass fishing is lagging with the falling water levels and prolific number of shad. Use electronics to find structure and stumps as bigger bass will be roaming looking for larger gizzard shad. Start fishing with topwaters in shallow water then gradually work out to deep water with slabs. Target striped bass with slabs under surfacing fish. Numbers of…
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is improving on topwaters and frogs first couple hours at day light. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Big groups of shad are coming in shallow as well for the bass to feed on. Largemouth bass are still in a summer pattern with an active bite on large topwaters, and dropshots on bluff walls and in the marinas. Look for bass to transition to fall locations in the coves as the weather cools.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on the move towards the deeper water but still holding in the brush with jigs and live minnows.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report

reports.text: Hybrids and white bass are good early in the morning at daylight on midlake points and drop offs along sandy flats throughout the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch and the spillway humps in 11-17 feet. Cast spinners and slabs and look for schooling fish on these flats as well as deeper seawalls and shorelines. Use spinnerbaits or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Hit up seawalls close to points in depths of 5-18 feet and cast rattle traps, spoons, slabs or sassy shads to get the hybrids to bite. The crappie bite has been getting better…

reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Cooler weather brought some good bass up to the shore, but the majority of fish are still out on the main lake.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing has improved to good with the best bite in the crappie house and deep brush piles with minnows. Bass are slow on deeper water ledges with crankbaits and soft plastics.
